## Findings
- claim-1: The supplied synopsis records the conjecture that both Schur generating sets are minimal, with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L12-L33|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: Assume the standard box model \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(q=n-r\), and \(J_v=\bigoplus_{\mu\supseteq i^j}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). If \(i=1\), put \(a=\min(q-1,r-j)\). Then \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline e_{j+t}. \] Consequently both families \[ \{s_{(t+1,1^{j-1})}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad \{s_{(1^{j+t})}:0\le t\le a\} \] map to integral bases and are irredundant generators of \(J_v\).
- claim-3: If \(j=1\), put \(a=\min(q-i,r-1)\). Then \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_{i+t}, \] and both families \[ \{s_{(i+t)}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad \{s_{(i,1^t)}:0\le t\le a\} \] map to integral bases and are irredundant.
## Strategy
Assume the box presentation
\[
A=\mathbb Z[h_1,\dots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\dots,e_{r+q}),\qquad A_+=(h_1,\dots,h_q),
\]
and the Schur-span description of \(J_v\).

For \(i=1\), set \(D=\min(r,j+q-1)=j+a\). Dual Jacobi–Trudi gives
\[
J_v=(e_j,\dots,e_r).
\]
Indeed, every \(s_\lambda\) with \(\ell(\lambda)\ge j\) expands along the first row of its dual Jacobi–Trudi determinant into the ideal generated by \(e_j,e_{j+1},\ldots\), and \(e_d=0\) in \(A\) for \(d>r\).

The recurrence from \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) gives, for \(d\ge j+q\),
\[
e_d\in A_+(e_j,\dots,e_{d-1})\subseteq A_+J_v.
\]
Thus \(Q:=J_v/A_+J_v\) is spanned by
\[
\bar e_j,\bar e_{j+1},\ldots,\bar e_D.
\]

For independence, prove over \(P_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q[h_1,\ldots,h_q]\) that
\[
e_j,\ldots,e_{j+q-1}
\]
is a regular sequence. Their common zero locus is only the origin: \(q\) consecutive zero coefficients of \(E(-t)=H(t)^{-1}\) force all later \(e_d\) to vanish by recurrence, so \(E(-t)\) is polynomial; then \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) forces \(H(t)=1\). Hence the quotient is finite-dimensional and nonzero, so these \(q\) homogeneous parameters are regular in the Cohen–Macaulay ring \(P_{\mathbb Q}\).

If \(j\le d\le D\) and \(z\bar e_d=0\) in \(Q\), degree considerations and the absence of box-kernel elements in degrees \(\le r\) yield
\[
ze_d\in(e_j,\ldots,e_{d-1})\subset P.
\]
After tensoring with \(\mathbb Q\), regularity contradicts \(z\ne0\). Since the candidate classes have distinct degrees, this proves
\[
Q\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\bar e_{j+t}.
\]

Dual Jacobi–Trudi for hooks gives
\[
s_{(t+1,1^{j-1})}\equiv(-1)^t e_{j+t}\pmod{A_+J_v}.
\]
Therefore both \(i=1\) proposed families map to integral bases of \(Q\), hence are irredundant by graded Nakayama.

For \(j=1\), use the integral involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), descending to
\[
A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r}.
\]
It exchanges \(h_d\) and \(e_d\), carries the \(i^1\)-ideal to the \(1^i\)-ideal, preserves positive-degree ideals, and transports the preceding result to
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\bar h_{i+t}.
\]

## Gaps
- This depends on the standard box presentation and the asserted identification of \(J_v\) with the Schur span of shapes containing \(i^j\).
- The regular-sequence, low-degree kernel, and hook-congruence arguments require independent line-by-line checking before being treated as a completed proof.
- No conclusion is obtained for \(b>1\).

## Next
- Independently audit the consecutive-\(e\) regular-sequence lemma and the integral torsion argument.
- Verify the \(\omega\)-descent and the dual Jacobi–Trudi hook sign.
- If these checks pass, record the uniform \(i=1\) and \(j=1\) cases as proved conditional on the box-model hypotheses.
